System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.TargetC.description: Construction Kit type ID that this archive captures time-series data for. A change is refused on an activated archive (AB#7872): it needs a new archive.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.Columns.description: Set of columns (attribute paths) the archive captures. At least one column is required. On an activated raw or time-range archive a column can be added; removing a column or changing its type is refused (AB#7872) and needs a new archive.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.Status-.description: Lifecycle status of the archive. Defaults to Created. Runtime-state (AB#4582): the lifecycle is operator-managed via ActivateArchive, not blueprint configuration. Marked isRuntimeState so a blueprint re-apply (InstallBlueprint -f) preserves the live status instead of resetting an activated archive back to the seeded Disabled/Created value and silently breaking stream-data queries.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.RawRete.description: Retention window for raw data points in milliseconds. When set, the partition pruner may drop source partitions older than (now - RawRetentionMs), but never ahead of the slowest attached rollup's watermark. Null means keep forever.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.FirstAc.description: When the archive was first seen activated (AB#7872): set by the platform when the archive is activated, or when it leaves Activated if it was activated before this attribute existed. Null on an archive that was never activated, which has no table yet. A disabled archive with this value is guarded like an activated one, because enabling it again would meet the same table.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.MaxRetr.description: Bounded retro reach (AB#4196): the maximum distance in milliseconds BEFORE the consumed watermark that a single retroactive write may drag an AUTOMATIC recompute of dependent rollups. A late write older than (consumedWatermark - MaxRetroactiveReachMs) is capped: only the in-reach tail schedules an automatic recompute, and the dropped older tail is audited so an operator can run an unbounded manual recomputeArchive if truly needed. This caps only automatic reach; manual recomputeArchive / rewindRollupWatermark stay unbounded. Null means unbounded (the pre-1.6.8 behaviour). Operator configuration, not runtime state; the effective cap is min(this, the host StreamData:Recompute:MaxRetroactiveReachHardLimitMs ceiling).

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.Conflic.description: Opt-in conflict resolution: an ordered list of keys that decides which of two competing writes to the SAME archive row survives. Empty or unset (the default, and the behaviour of every archive before System.StreamData 1.13.0) means last-write-wins: a re-delivered or out-of-order data point overwrites whatever is stored, so the stored value reflects arrival order rather than the data. With keys declared, the write that survives is the maximum of the total order the keys define — compared lexicographically, first key dominant — which is the same value whichever write lands first, so the result no longer depends on delivery order. That holds for writes the keys tell apart: two writes equal in every key are not ordered by them, and the later write replaces the stored row (an identical re-delivery stays an idempotent upsert). A stored row whose keys are null is always replaceable (rows written before the archive opted in carry none), and an incoming null key never displaces a stored non-null one. Name ingested columns carrying data the SOURCE decided, never the ingest time, which is arrival order again. Worked example, energy metering: [{DataQuality, LowerWins}, {SourceDocumentDate, HigherWins}] means a measured value is never displaced by an estimate, and two values of equal quality are ordered by their document date. Since 1.19.0 raw and time-range archives rank by the reserved key $Origin (row origin, manual above automated) first even when it is not listed, also when the list is empty: a manual write always wins and an automated one never replaces it. Listing $Origin explicitly places it where the author puts it (HigherWins), Order Ignore on $Origin opts the archive out of origin ranking, LowerWins on $Origin is refused. Rollup archives are unaffected.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.Status-.description: Lifecycle status of the archive. Defaults to Created. Runtime-state (AB#4582): the lifecycle is operator-managed via ActivateArchive, not blueprint configuration. Marked isRuntimeState so a blueprint re-apply (InstallBlueprint -f) preserves the live status instead of resetting an activated archive back to the seeded Disabled/Created value and silently breaking stream-data queries.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.RawRete.description: Retention window for raw data points in milliseconds. When set, the partition pruner may drop source partitions older than (now - RawRetentionMs), but never ahead of the slowest attached rollup's watermark. Null means keep forever.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.FirstAc.description: When the archive was first seen activated (AB#7872): set by the platform when the archive is activated, or when it leaves Activated if it was activated before this attribute existed. Null on an archive that was never activated, which has no table yet. A disabled archive with this value is guarded like an activated one, because enabling it again would meet the same table.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.MaxRetr.description: Bounded retro reach (AB#4196): the maximum distance in milliseconds BEFORE the consumed watermark that a single retroactive write may drag an AUTOMATIC recompute of dependent rollups. A late write older than (consumedWatermark - MaxRetroactiveReachMs) is capped: only the in-reach tail schedules an automatic recompute, and the dropped older tail is audited so an operator can run an unbounded manual recomputeArchive if truly needed. This caps only automatic reach; manual recomputeArchive / rewindRollupWatermark stay unbounded. Null means unbounded (the pre-1.6.8 behaviour). Operator configuration, not runtime state; the effective cap is min(this, the host StreamData:Recompute:MaxRetroactiveReachHardLimitMs ceiling).

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.Conflic.description: Opt-in conflict resolution: an ordered list of keys that decides which of two competing writes to the SAME archive row survives. Empty or unset (the default, and the behaviour of every archive before System.StreamData 1.13.0) means last-write-wins: a re-delivered or out-of-order data point overwrites whatever is stored, so the stored value reflects arrival order rather than the data. With keys declared, the write that survives is the maximum of the total order the keys define — compared lexicographically, first key dominant — which is the same value whichever write lands first, so the result no longer depends on delivery order. That holds for writes the keys tell apart: two writes equal in every key are not ordered by them, and the later write replaces the stored row (an identical re-delivery stays an idempotent upsert). A stored row whose keys are null is always replaceable (rows written before the archive opted in carry none), and an incoming null key never displaces a stored non-null one. Name ingested columns carrying data the SOURCE decided, never the ingest time, which is arrival order again. Worked example, energy metering: [{DataQuality, LowerWins}, {SourceDocumentDate, HigherWins}] means a measured value is never displaced by an estimate, and two values of equal quality are ordered by their document date. Since 1.19.0 raw and time-range archives rank by the reserved key $Origin (row origin, manual above automated) first even when it is not listed, also when the list is empty: a manual write always wins and an automated one never replaces it. Listing $Origin explicitly places it where the author puts it (HigherWins), Order Ignore on $Origin opts the archive out of origin ranking, LowerWins on $Origin is refused. Rollup archives are unaffected.

Must be positive and a multiple of the source rollup's bucket size when chaining. A change is refused on an activated rollup (AB#7872): it needs a new rollup. Int64 (AB#4281): calendar-month (2,419,200,000) and calendar-year (31,536,000,000) bucket widths exceed Int32.MaxValue (≈24.85 days), so the value type is 64-bit.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.W.description: Lower bound on how far behind real-time the orchestrator stays before closing a bucket, in milliseconds. Absorbs late-arriving source inserts. Default 300000 (five minutes). Can be changed on an activated rollup. Int64 (AB#4281) for consistency with BucketSizeMs — a lag can legitimately be sized against a calendar bucket.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.L.description: Exclusive end timestamp of the most recently committed bucket. Null before the first run. Maintained exclusively by the rollup orchestrator; manual edits go through the rewindRollupWatermark mutation. Runtime-state (AB#5232): blueprint seeds never declare a watermark, so without the flag a blueprint re-apply (InstallBlueprint -f) or plain ImportRt -r reset it to null and the orchestrator skipped the rollup forever ('watermark is null … Skipping until set').

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.A.description: List of aggregation definitions. At least one entry is required at activation time. A change is refused on an activated rollup (AB#7872): it needs a new rollup.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.F.description: When set, the rollup is read-only up to this timestamp: the orchestrator will not produce new buckets whose bucketEnd is ≤ FrozenUntil. Set automatically when the source archive is truncated for the covered range, so the already-aggregated history is preserved. Monotonic; can only move forward. Runtime-state (AB#5232): engine-written protection state, never part of a seed — a re-import clearing it would let the orchestrator recompute over the truncated source range and destroy the preserved history.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.B.description: Bucket-boundary alignment. FixedSize (default, key 0) preserves the legacy 'LastAggregatedBucketEnd + BucketSizeMs' arithmetic. Calendar/Iso8601 values align bucket boundaries to wall-clock UTC boundaries so monthly / weekly / yearly rollups become expressible without forcing BucketSizeMs into a single TimeSpan. Pre-1.4.0 entities resolve to FixedSize at read time. A change is refused on an activated rollup (AB#7872): it needs a new rollup.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.R.description: Optional IANA time-zone id (e.g. 'Europe/Vienna') used to align calendar bucket boundaries (day / week / month / year) to local wall-clock time so they are DST-correct across countries. Null (the default) keeps UTC calendar boundaries — the pre-1.6.4 behaviour. Only meaningful for calendar BucketAlignment variants; ignored for FixedSize. AB#4290 / decision O6. A change is refused on an activated rollup (AB#7872): it needs a new rollup.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.D.description: Optional local time of day at which a CalendarDay bucket starts, in milliseconds after local midnight of ReferenceTimeZone (AB#7358). 21600000 (06:00) with ReferenceTimeZone Europe/Vienna makes every bucket one gas day of 23, 24 or 25 hours. The offset is applied on the local wall clock, so the day start follows the zone across DST changes. Null or 0 = a midnight day (the behaviour before 1.22.0). Must be a whole number of minutes in [0, 86400000) and is only allowed with BucketAlignment CalendarDay. A rollup chained on an offset day rollup needs the same offset and ReferenceTimeZone, a week/month/quarter/year rollup cannot be chained on it. A change is refused on an activated rollup: it needs a new rollup.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.C.description: How far before a bucket's start the TimeWeightedAvg carry-in scan (last observation carried forward) looks for the opening state, in milliseconds. Bounds the per-bucket source scan; a signal silent for longer than this loses its carry and the bucket becomes partially covered. Null (the default) uses the engine default of 35 days. Only consulted by TimeWeightedAvg aggregations; ignored otherwise. Mutable. AB#4336 / decision D1.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/RollupArchive.L.description: Why the last run of the rollup orchestrator failed (AB#7872). Null while the rollup runs. Set by the orchestrator together with LastRunErrorAt and ConsecutiveRunFailures, cleared by the next run that succeeds. The rollup keeps its status and is retried on every tick; a rollup that keeps failing does not advance.

Null on an archive that was never activated, which has no table yet. A disabled archive with this value is guarded like an activated one, because enabling it again would meet the same table.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.MaxRetr.description: Bounded retro reach (AB#4196): the maximum distance in milliseconds BEFORE the consumed watermark that a single retroactive write may drag an AUTOMATIC recompute of dependent rollups. A late write older than (consumedWatermark - MaxRetroactiveReachMs) is capped: only the in-reach tail schedules an automatic recompute, and the dropped older tail is audited so an operator can run an unbounded manual recomputeArchive if truly needed. This caps only automatic reach; manual recomputeArchive / rewindRollupWatermark stay unbounded. Null means unbounded (the pre-1.6.8 behaviour). Operator configuration, not runtime state; the effective cap is min(this, the host StreamData:Recompute:MaxRetroactiveReachHardLimitMs ceiling).

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.Conflic.description: Opt-in conflict resolution: an ordered list of keys that decides which of two competing writes to the SAME archive row survives. Empty or unset (the default, and the behaviour of every archive before System.StreamData 1.13.0) means last-write-wins: a re-delivered or out-of-order data point overwrites whatever is stored, so the stored value reflects arrival order rather than the data. With keys declared, the write that survives is the maximum of the total order the keys define — compared lexicographically, first key dominant — which is the same value whichever write lands first, so the result no longer depends on delivery order. That holds for writes the keys tell apart: two writes equal in every key are not ordered by them, and the later write replaces the stored row (an identical re-delivery stays an idempotent upsert). A stored row whose keys are null is always replaceable (rows written before the archive opted in carry none), and an incoming null key never displaces a stored non-null one. Name ingested columns carrying data the SOURCE decided, never the ingest time, which is arrival order again. Worked example, energy metering: [{DataQuality, LowerWins}, {SourceDocumentDate, HigherWins}] means a measured value is never displaced by an estimate, and two values of equal quality are ordered by their document date. Since 1.19.0 raw and time-range archives rank by the reserved key $Origin (row origin, manual above automated) first even when it is not listed, also when the list is empty: a manual write always wins and an automated one never replaces it. Listing $Origin explicitly places it where the author puts it (HigherWins), Order Ignore on $Origin opts the archive out of origin ranking, LowerWins on $Origin is refused. Rollup archives are unaffected.

Null on an archive that was never activated, which has no table yet. A disabled archive with this value is guarded like an activated one, because enabling it again would meet the same table.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.MaxRetr.description: Bounded retro reach (AB#4196): the maximum distance in milliseconds BEFORE the consumed watermark that a single retroactive write may drag an AUTOMATIC recompute of dependent rollups. A late write older than (consumedWatermark - MaxRetroactiveReachMs) is capped: only the in-reach tail schedules an automatic recompute, and the dropped older tail is audited so an operator can run an unbounded manual recomputeArchive if truly needed. This caps only automatic reach; manual recomputeArchive / rewindRollupWatermark stay unbounded. Null means unbounded (the pre-1.6.8 behaviour). Operator configuration, not runtime state; the effective cap is min(this, the host StreamData:Recompute:MaxRetroactiveReachHardLimitMs ceiling).

System.StreamData-1.30.0/Archive.Conflic.description: Opt-in conflict resolution: an ordered list of keys that decides which of two competing writes to the SAME archive row survives. Empty or unset (the default, and the behaviour of every archive before System.StreamData 1.13.0) means last-write-wins: a re-delivered or out-of-order data point overwrites whatever is stored, so the stored value reflects arrival order rather than the data. With keys declared, the write that survives is the maximum of the total order the keys define — compared lexicographically, first key dominant — which is the same value whichever write lands first, so the result no longer depends on delivery order. That holds for writes the keys tell apart: two writes equal in every key are not ordered by them, and the later write replaces the stored row (an identical re-delivery stays an idempotent upsert). A stored row whose keys are null is always replaceable (rows written before the archive opted in carry none), and an incoming null key never displaces a stored non-null one. Name ingested columns carrying data the SOURCE decided, never the ingest time, which is arrival order again. Worked example, energy metering: [{DataQuality, LowerWins}, {SourceDocumentDate, HigherWins}] means a measured value is never displaced by an estimate, and two values of equal quality are ordered by their document date. Since 1.19.0 raw and time-range archives rank by the reserved key $Origin (row origin, manual above automated) first even when it is not listed, also when the list is empty: a manual write always wins and an automated one never replaces it. Listing $Origin explicitly places it where the author puts it (HigherWins), Order Ignore on $Origin opts the archive out of origin ranking, LowerWins on $Origin is refused. Rollup archives are unaffected.

records.description: One key of an archive's conflict precedence. The keys are compared in declaration order, lexicographically: the first key decides, and a later key only breaks a tie in every key before it. That ordering is what makes the outcome independent of the order writes arrive in — the surviving value is the maximum of a total order over the competing writes, which is the same whichever one is written first. Two writes that are equal in every key are not ordered by them: the later write replaces the stored row, so the keys have to tell apart every pair of writes that can carry different values. Name a column of this archive; Order says which direction of it counts as better.

Which direction of this key counts as better.

records.description: Information A of the recompute model (AB#4184): a window on a source archive whose data changed retroactively. Through which path the change arrived (Manual / Pipeline / Import).
When the storage layer detected and recorded the change (UTC).

The distinct rtIds (metering points / streams) whose rows made the window dirty (AB#9016). The recompute of the dependent rollups is restricted to exactly these series. Empty or missing means every series in the window, as before 1.26.0; the storage layer leaves it empty when a write touches more rtIds than StreamData:Recompute:MaxScopedRtIds.

records.description: Information B of the recompute model (AB#4184): one pending recompute obligation, derived by propagating a dirty window through the rollup dependency graph. Identifies a dependent archive and the bucket-aligned range to recompute, optionally scoped to a single rtId. Held on the source archive's ledger until the recompute orchestrator picks it up.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/CkArchiveRecomp.description: Runtime id of the dependent archive that must be recomputed for this range.
Inclusive, bucket-aligned start of the range to recompute on the dependent (UTC).
Exclusive, bucket-aligned end of the range to recompute on the dependent (UTC).
Optional single rtId (metering point / stream) the recompute is restricted to. Null means all rtIds in the range.

Optional set of rtIds the recompute is restricted to (AB#9016), carried over from the dirty window of a late delivery and inherited by the chained dependents. The orchestrator refreshes only these series in place at the bucket's active generation. Empty or missing means no set scope (RtIdScope or all rtIds).

How many times a recompute of this range has already failed (AB#5189). Zero on a freshly enqueued obligation; incremented each time the drain re-enqueues the range after a failure. Once it reaches the orchestrator's MaxRangeAttempts the obligation is parked (NextAttemptAt far in the future) instead of retried forever, and LastError explains why.

Earliest UTC time the drain may retry this range (AB#5189). Set to an exponentially backed-off point in time after each failure so a permanently broken rollup stops consuming a recompute run every tick; set to the year 9999 once the attempt cap is reached, which parks the obligation until a recompute covering it succeeds. Null means retry on the next tick.

Error message of the most recent failed attempt at this range (AB#5189). Null while the obligation has never failed. Kept per range so an operator can tell which part of a partially recomputed range is stuck and why.

records.description: Single aggregation definition for a CkRollupArchive. Maps a source archive column (SourcePath) to one or more storage columns via Function. AVG materialises as two stored columns (sum + count); the other functions map 1:1.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/CkRollupAggrega.description: Attribute path on the source archive (must exist in the source's Columns list at activation time). For chained rollups referencing a stored AVG, use the explicit _sum / _count column names.

Optional explicit storage column name. Default is '{sourcePath}_{function}' lower-cased; for AVG, two columns are created with suffixes _sum and _count derived from this base name.

records.description: One source archive of a RollupArchive together with its optional validity span (AB#5157). A rollup may declare several time-disjoint sources so that history imported at a coarser granularity and data ingested natively at a finer granularity end up in one continuous rollup ladder. ValidFrom is inclusive, ValidTo is exclusive; a reference without bounds is unbounded. Spans must be pairwise disjoint and every boundary must lie on a bucket boundary of the rollup, so every bucket lies entirely within one source's span or within none.

System.StreamData-1.30.0/CkRollupSourceR.description: Runtime id of one source Archive this rollup aggregates from. May reference another RollupArchive to form a chain (e.g. raw → 1 min → 1 h). Each source archive may appear at most once in a rollup's Sources list. AB#5157.

Inclusive start of the span in which this source is authoritative. Null means an open start — the source covers every bucket before its ValidTo. Must lie on a bucket boundary of the rollup in its reference time zone, and must be earlier than ValidTo when both are set. AB#5157.

Exclusive end of the span in which this source is authoritative. Null means an open end — the source covers every bucket from its ValidFrom onwards. Must lie on a bucket boundary of the rollup in its reference time zone. A bucket no span covers stays empty and the watermark advances. AB#5157.

values.description: A backfill has been scheduled for this computed column but has not started yet. Consumers still see the previous archive state.

values.description: The backfill is running. Consumers still see the previous archive state until it completes and is committed atomically.

values.name: HigherWins
values.description: The greater value is the better one. Use for timestamps, sequence numbers and versions, where later or higher supersedes earlier.

values.name: LowerWins
values.description: The smaller value is the better one. Use for rank-like codes numbered best-first, where a lower code must never be displaced by a higher one.

values.name: Ignore
values.description: Only valid on the reserved key $Origin: the archive opts out of ranking by row origin, so a manual value has no priority and the other keys (or the last write) decide. Without it, raw and time-range archives always rank by $Origin first. Refused on a column key.

enums.description: Which direction of a conflict-precedence key counts as better, i.e. which of two competing values for the same archive row is allowed to survive. Needed because 'better' is domain-specific and not always 'larger': a document timestamp orders by recency (higher wins), while a quality or priority code is usually numbered best-first (lower wins, e.g. an OBIS data quality where 1 = measured and 3 = estimated).

values.name: Append
values.description: A forward write at or after the high-water mark already consumed by dependents. Does not, by itself, make a dependent stale.

values.name: RetroactiveModify

enums.description: How a write touched an archive window, used to drive recompute of derived archives (AB#4184). Append is a normal forward write past the consumed high-water mark; RetroactiveModify is a correction / late value / re-ingest into an already-consumed window and is what marks dependents dirty.

values.name: Manual
values.description: An operator changed the data directly (manual correction).

values.name: Pipeline
values.description: A mesh-adapter pipeline re-ingested or corrected the data (e.g. a corrected DATEN_CRMSG from EDA).

values.name: Import

enums.description: Through which path a retroactive archive change arrived (AB#4184). Kept separately from CkRecomputeChangeKind so the audit trail can distinguish a manual operator edit from an automated pipeline re-ingest or a bulk import.

values.name: Running

values.name: Swapping
values.description: Staging is complete and the atomic commit (full-archive SWAP TABLE or per-window generation-pointer flip) is in progress.

values.name: Completed
values.description: The recompute committed atomically; readers now see the new values.

values.name: Failed
values.description: The job failed before committing. Staging is discarded; the previous archive state is intact and consumers never saw a partial result.

values.name: Coalesced
values.description: The triggering request was merged into an already-active job for the same archive (its range was folded into that job).

enums.description: Lifecycle state of a single archive recompute run (AB#4184). Engine-managed. values.name: Manual
values.description: An operator forced the recompute via API / admin UI / octo-cli.

values.name: Periodic

models.description: Core system model library providing foundational types for entity management, multi-tenant configuration, auto-increment sequences, a comprehensive query system with support for filtering/sorting/aggregations/text-search, the System/TimeRange record used by stream-data archives, and per-tenant blueprint registry types (Installation/History/Backup) that track which blueprints have been applied.

StreamData model. Defines the abstract Archive base, RawArchive (instant measurements), RollupArchive (derived bucketed-aggregation archives), TimeRangeArchive (externally pre-aggregated [from, to) windowed data), and supporting enum/record types. 1.1.0 → 1.2.0 renamed CkArchive → Archive (abstract) + introduced RawArchive; Every archive write is an upsert on the row key (raw: timestamp + rtid + ckTypeId; windowed: window_start + window_end + rtid + ckTypeId), and until now the update was unconditional, so a re-delivered or out-of-order data point silently replaced newer stored values with older ones — the stored value reflected ARRIVAL order, not the data. ConflictPrecedence declares an ordered list of keys, each naming one of the archive's own columns plus which direction of it counts as better (HigherWins for timestamps and sequence numbers, LowerWins for rank-like codes numbered best-first); competing writes are compared lexicographically, first key dominant, and the better one survives. Because that is a total order over the data itself, the outcome is the same whichever write lands first — delivery order stops mattering rather than merely being satisfied, which is what lets a producer stop pre-sorting its input. Writes that are equal in every key are not ordered by it; the later write replaces the stored row. A single-column form of this (Archive.ConflictVersionColumn, one comparable column, newest wins) was tried first and superseded before publication: a full replay of a productive energy tenant showed it is not enough, because a later ESTIMATE then overwrites an earlier MEASUREMENT — 22 of 805 days came out wrong, and with billing counting measured intervals only, such a day bills as zero. Two keys express the rule correctly ([{DataQuality, LowerWins}, {SourceDocumentDate, HigherWins}]), and generalising to a list rather than hard-coding quality keeps the mechanism usable for any domain that ranks its data.
